title: Implement clean authz v2 atomic cutover
description:
## Implementation
Continued Authz v2 clean-cutover classification. Slice 50 adds exact self authorization for current-user hospital context, notification listing, and mark-all-read. Notification-by-ID and recipient-targeted routes remain fail-closed pending ownership/target binders. Filtering and read-state behavior remain application code.

## Verification
Combined focused run: 1104 passed. Inventory: 594 explicit Authz v2 routes, 47 legacy-unmapped routes. Core and domain-boundary tests pass.
design: Freeze pure core and facade contracts first; build persistence/repositories and Flask/API infrastructure against those contracts; migrate vertical feature slices only after the shared contract gate; perform one release cutover that leaves only authz/. Parent agent owns integration, route manifest, migration ordering, full validation, and push.
acceptance_criteria: All completion gates in docs/15-DEVELOPMENT/authz_v2_clean_cutover_plan.md pass: one authz package, no legacy decision engine or final-control role/bypass checks, every endpoint classified, exact checks and SQL list scoping agree, mandatory audit and ID-only migration verified, API/docs updated, Docker tests and static bypass scan pass, final code-quality audit has no material finding.
notes: 2026-08-28 vertical slice 3: migrated all 16 encounter-set and 14 Remidio verification routes, reducing unmapped runtime consumers to 603 (556 HTTP, 47 Celery). Added least-privilege verification.encounter_set.view so reads do not borrow update authority. Exact encounter/image resources are mandatory; missing body-only identifiers deny. Verification: 728 authz_v2/app_init tests passed; generated policy parity, Ruff, Bandit, and diff checks passed. Next: mobile clinical APIs and upload/inference/job surfaces.

title: Grant verifier to every data_manager holder before verification narrows
description:
Prerequisite operational grant for the verification narrowing (divergence D-7).

VERIFICATION_ROLES is currently {verifier, admin, local_admin, fileUploader, data_manager} and narrows to {verifier, admin}. At audit time, five active data_manager holders lacked verifier; three additional users who verified through fileUploader alone were deliberately outside the grant.

## Implementation
Run a one-time, assertion-guarded query selecting active users who hold data_manager and lack verifier. Do not select by username and do not grant verifier to fileUploader-only users.

## Ordering
Run this before the role set narrows, or the eligible users lose verification access at cutover.

## Verification
The eligible preflight count is exactly five; all five grants are inserted; no active data_manager remains without verifier. See docs/policy/authorizations.md, divergence D-7.
notes: Applied through the Compose web service as a one-time transactional role-based query. Preconditions required exactly five active data_manager users missing verifier. Postconditions confirmed five grants and zero active data_manager users still missing verifier. No username-dependent migration or tracked operational script was created.
close_reason: Applied and verified the role-based prerequisite grant without a tracked username-dependent migration

title: AUTHZ-02: legacy EncounterSet grading bypasses allocation and trusts the client-supplied slot
description:
From docs/audit/AUTHZ_SURFACE_ROUTE_AUDIT_2026-08-25.md, severity Critical, confirmed still live 2026-08-26.

grading/encounter_set_grading.py, registered at grading/__init__.py:58, guarded only by roles_required('resident2','ophthalmologist','arbitrator','admin') at :33 and :93.

GET loads a task by UUID and reveals its encounter and all images with no allocation check (:36-73).
POST accepts task_uuid and slot from the browser (:100), validates slot only for set membership (:112), then assigns role_slot = slot (:114) and writes the grade under the client's chosen slot (:139), recomputing task state and consensus (:149-152). label_id is accepted without proving it exists, is active, or belongs to the task's disease.

Net effect: any holder of those four roles can alter an arbitrary reachable task and its consensus outside their assigned step. This is a parallel transport that does not consult the allocation checks the workbench path enforces.

## Remediation
Retire this transport, or delegate both GET and POST through the canonical workbench service: derive the permitted slot server-side, validate the label against the task's disease, and authorize the task before revealing images or writing a grade.
notes:
Fixed 2026-08-26 by DELETING the transport, per the recommendation in both this audit and docs/audit/PERMISSIONS_SCOPING_AUDIT_2026-08.md.

Caller analysis first: there is no url_for('grading.encounter_set_grading') anywhere in the codebase. The only production reference was the form at templates/grading/encounter_set_grading.html:180 - inside the template the GET route renders itself. So the pair was reachable only by typing or bookmarking the URL. User confirmed only the workbench model is in use.

Removed: grading/encounter_set_grading.py, templates/grading/encounter_set_grading.html, and the registration in grading/__init__.py. Verified /grading/encounter_set/<uuid> and /grading/encounter_set/submit are gone from the URL map.

Chose deletion over patching because the workbench already derives the slot server-side and checks allocation exactly. Patching would have meant reimplementing allocation resolution, slot derivation and label validation in a second place - the drift that created this finding.

Tests: removed the 10 route-dependent tests from tests/integration/test_encounter_set_grading.py and the obsolete TestCSRFProtectionGrading class. Kept the 4 that never depended on the transport (task creation x3, media serving). No coverage lost: submission is covered by test_ordinary_submission_commits_grade_annotation_set_audit_and_lease_release and consensus by test_workbench_state_machine_owns_match_consensus, both in tests/unit/grading/test_workbench_submission.py.

Regression: 510 passed, 17 failed, 19 errors across grading, grading_allocation, authz, api, security and the trimmed integration file. The 17 failures are the same pre-existing set as before; errors went 20 -> 19 because the obsolete CSRF test was removed.
close_reason: Legacy transport deleted; it had no callers and the workbench supersedes it with exact allocation checks

title: AUTHZ-01: /dashboard/* is login-only and globally unscoped (cross-hospital read + export)
description:
From docs/audit/AUTHZ_SURFACE_ROUTE_AUDIT_2026-08-25.md, severity Critical, confirmed still live 2026-08-26.

dashboard/routes.py has NO authorization decorators. All three routes are registered bare in dashboard/__init__.py:9-11:
  GET /dashboard/
  GET /dashboard/hospital/<hospital_id>
  GET /dashboard/images  (+ ?export=csv, ?export=excel)

The app-wide guard in app.py establishes authentication only. Any active authenticated account, any role, any hospital, can read cross-hospital data and export image UUIDs, filenames, facility metadata, encounter dates and glaucoma/VCDR fields.

Conflicts with docs/policy/authorizations.md:661-665 which requires an accepted dashboard role plus classical scope for dashboard.view. An executable dashboard.view policy already exists; these routes simply do not consume it.

## Remediation
Wire all three routes to the dashboard action and scope every hospital/image query before rendering or exporting. Export must reuse the same filtered query as the page.
notes:
Fixed 2026-08-26 in dashboard/routes.py.

_dashboard_scope() authorizes dashboard.view PER LAB UNIT through the authz engine and returns the allowed (lab_unit_ids, hospital_ids). Per-lab was necessary, not stylistic: dashboard.view is _general(CLINICAL_READ_ROLES) with GENERAL_SCOPE_GRANTS, and engine._matches_lab_unit compares resource.attr('lab_unit_id') against the grant, so authorize() with no ResourceRef can never match a lab grant and always returns missing_relationship. Asking per lab unit makes the engine the source of truth and the scope falls out of its answers: ADMIN_GLOBAL matches every lab, HOSPITAL_SCOPE its hospital's labs, LAB_UNIT_ASSIGNMENT the assigned ones.

Fails closed twice: anonymous -> 401, empty allowed set -> 403 (never 'no filter').

Scoping applied:
- hospital_dashboard: hospitals filtered to hospital_ids; user and image counts constrained to lab_unit_ids.
- hospital_detail: out-of-scope hospital returns the same 404 as a missing one (non-disclosing); lab units filtered.
- image_list: scope applied to the BASE direct/encounter queries before search, pagination and export branch off them, so export cannot widen the page's selection. Grade lookups derive from the already-filtered image ids.

Also removed a duplicated import block mid-file, and stopped resolving scope through upload_profiles.service.get_user_lab_unit_ids, which opened its own session (contrary to the project's one-session-per-request rule and invisible to the request's transaction).

Tests: tests/security/test_dashboard_authz.py, 6 passing - no-scope denial, cross-hospital hiding, non-disclosing detail, export scoping (csv + xlsx), and admin retaining full visibility.

Regression check: tests/unit/authz + grading + grading_allocation + api + security = 504 passed, 17 failed, 20 errors; all 17 and all 20 reproduce on a clean tree. One pre-existing test (test_dashboard_image_list_export_anonymization) had to be given a login: it exercised the export with NO authenticated user and previously got data back, which is AUTHZ-01 itself.
close_reason: Dashboard routes now authorize dashboard.view per lab unit and scope every query including export; 6 regression tests added

title: Fix 20 authorization findings from route-by-route audit
description:
Twenty authorization findings from the route-by-route audit.

## Implementation

Cross-hospital IDOR / fail-open scoping
- H8/H9 glaucoma_unverify, nodr_unverify: lab-unit check added after loading the encounter, 403 for AJAX.
- M16 screenings (4 guards): 'encounter.lab_unit_id and allowed and ...' passed when either side was empty. Now fails closed; prev/next navigation scoped to the same labs.
- M17 verify_remedio_dr/glaucoma/nodr: 'lab_unit_id is not None and' and 'if encounter:' guards let NULL-lab and orphaned rows through. Guards now compare unconditionally.
- H11 direct-files KPI: lab filter was only applied when the set was non-empty, and kpiutils returns an empty set on any exception. Filter is now unconditional.
- L23 threshold explorer: added the 'AND 1=0' fallback the GET route already had.

Dataset curation
- H10 dataset_detail POST: form task_id written with no scope or disease check. Now loaded through scope() and matched against dataset.disease_id.
- M18 toggle-item: no dataset gate, and mutation preceded the scoped lookup (get_db_session commits on early return). Gate and lookup now precede the write.
- M19 dataset export: dropped the dataset_creator role exemption; task_ids re-scoped at export time.
- L22 dataset listing: was unscoped across hospitals; now gated on filters_json.allowed_lab_units.

User administration
- M1 users_update: no hospital check (unlike edit_user), and no protection for admin accounts. Both added.
- M2 add_user: lab units attached without hospital validation.
- L12 add_user: transaction_scope commits on normal exit, so a rejected request still created the user. All validation moved before db.add(user).

Other
- M14 intra-rater: scope checks were conditional on lab_unit_id. allowed_lab_unit_ids now threaded through candidate selection and grader eligibility.
- M15 jobs: NULL-lab jobs were visible to any job-role holder, and export jobs are always NULL-lab. Shared _job_visible() rule; regenerate_export re-applies the dataset gate.
- M20 encounter export: scoped by reachable labs only, never intersected with project grants. scope(PatientEncounters, 'analytics.encounters.view') applied.
- M9 open redirect in confirm_password: next validated with is_safe_url.
- L8 ILIKE wildcard injection (4 sites): new escape_like() helper in utils/log_sanitize.py.
- L11 startswith path containment replaced with relative_to.
- L15 user-existence oracle: authorize before lookup.
- L17 deleted unregistered setup_thumbnail_routes.
- L18 grading allocation: actor lab units now intersected with the project's configured labs.
- L20 bulk_edit: hospital validated for every non-admin role, not just local_admin.
- L21 rejected-submission audit: no row written for an unknown session uuid; project_annotations decorator listed slot names as roles.
- Bug: api/encounter_set.py used url_for without importing it (500 on the details endpoint).

Also: declared pytest-timeout in pyproject.toml (was installed but undeclared, so it vanished on rebuild).

## Verification

Full suite before/after with an identical selection, comparing failure sets rather than counts:
docker compose exec -T -u $(id -u):$(id -g) -e UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/.uv-cache web uv run pytest tests/ -q -p no:randomly --ignore=tests/e2e --ignore=tests/regression/bugs/test_bug_2026_01_nat_encoding.py --ignore=tests/unit/remote_inference/test_madhunetra_migration.py

Baseline: 127 failed, 1626 passed, 74 errors.
After:    127 failed, 1626 passed, 74 errors.
Failure sets identical (comm -13 and comm -23 both empty).

One regression was caught and fixed during this: the screenings prev/next helper was wrapping .first() instead of the query.

Excluded from the run and why: tests/e2e (playwright not installed), test_bug_2026_01_nat_encoding.py (missing tests.test_auth_helpers) -- both fail collection on main; test_madhunetra_migration.py times out only in a full run (passes alone in 7s, known test-db lock interference).

App boot verified: 677 routes register.

title: Admin routes reachable by any authenticated user (authz regression)
description:
29 routes on admin_bp have no role check. Regression from 427550be (2025-09-04) which moved admin routes from @admin_bp.route+@roles_required to add_url_rule() and dropped the decorators.

Confirmed by runtime probe as user with only discrepancy_reviewer+ophthalmologist roles:
- POST /admin/change-password resets ANY user password and returns it in the response (admin/security.py:15) -> full account takeover
- POST /admin/users/new creates users with roles (admin/users.py:271) -> privilege escalation
- GET /admin/users, /admin/users/<id> -> bulk staff PII
- delete/edit for hospital, lab_unit, disease, camera, area -> destructive master-data ops (all returned 302 not 403)
- /admin/roles, /admin/malicious-uploads

Affects production (present on main).

## Fix
1. Add explicit @roles_required to the 29 undecorated views.
2. Add admin_bp.before_request coarse gate (mirroring admin/database_restore.py:90) so default is deny.

## Verification
Re-run low-privilege probe; all must return 403.
close_reason: Fixed in 036d7891: restored roles_required on 29 admin_bp views (lookups, users, security, uploads). Verified by low-privilege probe - all previously-reachable routes now 403, admin access unchanged. malicious_uploads (h8n) covered by the same commit.

title: Migration 86eca6cd0465 (encrypt_existing_smtp_passwords) is empty - SMTP passwords not encrypted
description:
## ✅ RESOLVED: Not Applicable - No Production Deployment

### Issue Summary
Migration `86eca6cd0465_encrypt_existing_smtp_passwords_in_.py` was created with empty `upgrade()` and `downgrade()` functions (just `pass`).

### Verification Results
1. **No email_settings records exist** - app not deployed yet
2. **New passwords ARE encrypted** - verified code flow:
   - `create_email_settings()` calls `set_password()` at `utils/email_config.py:314`
   - `update_email_settings()` calls `set_password()` at `utils/email_config.py:363`
   - Encryption uses `cryptography.fernet.Fernet` (AES-128-CBC with HMAC)
   - Each record gets unique `password_salt` for per-record encryption

### Root Cause
Migration was meant to encrypt existing plaintext passwords from before encryption was implemented. Since app hasn't been deployed, no legacy passwords exist.

### Resolution
**NOT A BUG** - Empty migration is acceptable because:
- No email_settings records in database
- New passwords properly encrypted via `set_password()` method
- No legacy plaintext passwords to migrate
- Encryption working correctly for future records

### Migration Note
The empty migration `86eca6cd0465` can be left as-is. If existing plaintext passwords are ever discovered, a new fix migration can be created.
close_reason: Resolved: Not applicable - no production deployment, new passwords are properly encrypted via set_password() method

title: Build the truthful authz route-gate foundation
description:
Foundation split from fundus_img_xtract-guz4. A literal @requires(action) cannot authorize resource-required routes or scope collections without route-specific canonical resolution. Build the shared decorator and typed contracts first, then migrate domains incrementally.

## Implementation
Add authz route contracts and @requires. Validate action at decoration time; reject resource-required actions without a resolver; resolve session principal and grants before handler invocation; accept canonical ResourceRef plus supplemental resource-bound grants; deny before handler execution; expose the authorized context on Flask g; attach action/enforcement metadata to the actual registered wrapper. Leave collection scoping as an explicit unsupported mode until its separate contract lands.

## Verification
Unit tests prove unknown actions and missing resolvers fail closed, public actions avoid DB resolution, authenticated self/resource-free actions resolve grants, resource resolvers use canonical references, denial and resolver failure prevent handler invocation, and wrapper metadata is present. Run the complete Docker authz unit suite.
acceptance_criteria: The shared @requires gate is fail-closed, resource-aware, metadata-bearing, and test-proven to execute before handlers; it makes no unsupported collection-scope claim.

title: Reconcile ICMR-VG grading tasks outside the configured project lab boundary
description:
Read-only allocation verification found 36 target-resolvable open ICMR-VG tasks assigned to lab unit 3 while the project has only lab unit 1 configured as active. Twelve are on one disease-specific target and twenty-four on the other. All project allocations are correctly confined to lab unit 1, so the 36 tasks are unavailable and blindly adding lab-3 allocations would widen authority beyond the configured project boundary.

## Implementation
Determine whether the task lab attribution is wrong or the project lab configuration is incomplete. Correct the authoritative source and rebuild/re-home affected tasks as appropriate; do not grant outside the project boundary as a workaround.

## Verification
No open project task has a lab_unit_id outside its project active lab-unit set, and the 36 affected tasks are reachable only through the corrected in-boundary allocation context.
acceptance_criteria: Every open ICMR-VG task is within an active project lab boundary and target-resolvable; no allocation is created outside that boundary.

title: Enforced project grading tasks fail closed without an allocation target
description:
Four projects currently enforce explicit grader allocations. Read-only runtime resolution found 7,225 open project-owned grading tasks whose allocation target resolves to none: 1,093 in GLAU_SCR_APP, 6,130 in ICMR-VG, and 1 in SEVA PRISTINE. These tasks cannot match any ProjectGraderAllocation, regardless of how many rows are backfilled, and therefore fail closed under enforced allocation.

## Implementation
Classify the target-none tasks by source shape and determine whether they are stale work to retire, missing frozen package target metadata, or resolver gaps. Repair or retire them without weakening fail-closed behavior.

## Verification
For each enforcement-enabled project, every open task either resolves a currently valid semantic target or is deliberately retired with an auditable reason. Re-run the allocation resolver audit and require target-none count zero for live open tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Every live open task in an enforcement-enabled project resolves a valid allocation target; deliberately retired tasks are auditable; resolver remains fail closed.

title: Per-Lab-Unit site settings, and separating grade columns from encounter columns in exports
description:
Divergence D-48 and D-45. Two halves: a new setting, and the export rework it needs.

## The settings
Three flags per (project, Lab Unit) pair, on ProjectLabUnit, which today carries only project_id, lab_unit_id and active:
- sites_can_export_grades
- sites_can_create_datasets
- sites_can_share_datasets

Per pair rather than per project: a study may trust one site with work it withholds from another, and a Lab Unit serving two projects may sit under different terms in each. All default OFF.

They govern every lab-unit-scoped holder at that Lab Unit -- operational roles AND site_pi. They constrain and never confer: turning one on removes a restriction from holders who already have the role; it grants nobody anything. A project-wide holder is unaffected.

Each needs the setting AND the role, neither substituting:
- grade export: sites_can_export_grades + data_exporter
- dataset creation: sites_can_create_datasets + dataset_creator
- dataset sharing: sites_can_share_datasets + data_exporter

Do NOT reuse ProjectEncounterSetPermission.can_export_data / can_create_datasets. Those are per-USER legacy capability grants (the LEGACY_PROJECT_CAPABILITY source that fundus_img_xtract-xwwk retires), not settings on a site.

## The export rework (D-45)
A site always exports its own encounters, images and captured data. What is withheld by default is the GRADES -- the readings human graders produced on that data, which are the project's clinical output rather than the site's record of what it captured.

The current export paths cannot express that. utils/dataframeEncounterFiles.py emits dr_result, dr_qualitative_result, glaucoma_result, glaucoma_qualitative_result, glaucoma_vcdr_right_num and glaucoma_vcdr_left_num in the SAME ROW as the encounter's own fields. So withholding grades is not a permission check on the current export -- it is a change to what the dataframe emits.

Rework so grade columns are separable from encounter columns, then gate the grade columns on the setting plus data_exporter. Applies to /kpis/encounter-files/filtered-dataframe and its Excel variant.

Note this compounds fundus_img_xtract-1rs2, which already requires patient_id and zip_filename to be maskable in the same exports. Sequence them together: one pass over the export column model rather than two.

## Verification
Tests: a lab-unit-scoped data_exporter at a Lab Unit with the setting off receives encounter columns and no grade columns; with it on, receives both; a project-wide holder is unaffected either way; site_pi at a Lab Unit with the setting off cannot export grades. Assert the same person holding grants at two Lab Units gets different results per Lab Unit.

See docs/policy/authorizations.md, 'A project decides what each of its sites may do'.

title: KPI exports leak patient identifiers and are closed to project users
description:
From the per-action audit of the analytics/KPI surface (finding 3).

## Identifier leak
analytics.kpi.encounter_files.rows carries shows_pii=False, but /kpis/encounter-files/filtered-dataframe and its Excel variant export 32 columns per encounter including:
- patient_id -- the clinic patient number, a direct identifier (4,272 distinct across 4,489 encounters)
- zip_filename -- MEASURED: contains patient_id in 2,191 of 2,191 rows, i.e. 100%. This is the Remedio naming convention, not an accident. Dropping patient_id alone does NOT close the leak; a column review would clear zip_filename on its name.
- dr_result, glaucoma_result, vcdr_right/left -- clinical findings, per patient
- verification_remarks -- unbounded free text, cannot be sanitised by column review
- encounter_verified_by / dr_verified_by / glaucoma_verified_by, uploader_full_name -- staff personal data

Verified clean: encounter_files.filename (0/6,365), encounter_file_pdfs.filename (0/1,947), and patient name appears in no filename.

## Ruling (2026-08-26): mask by authority, via SEPARATE ACTIONS
Not role-conditioned masking. f9e3ffa8 moved disclosure from actor to action for a measured reason (7 of 21 users unmasked everywhere because masking took the weakest role); do not reintroduce it.
- Ordinary export action: shows_pii=False, emits patient_id and zip_filename masked.
- New identifier-bearing action: shows_pii=True, requires the new pii_exporter role IN ADDITION to the role authorizing the export. data_exporter decides whether you may release; pii_exporter decides whether identifiers are included. Neither substitutes for the other. pii_exporter is held on the project, since release carries project scope.

## Enable for projects
- encounter-files already has the project branch (actions with .view/.rows plus scope()). It is blocked only by the route gate @roles_required('admin','data_manager'), which admits 2 roles against an action set of 9 -- analytics_viewer, the role whose stated purpose is reading KPIs, reaches no KPI endpoint at all, nor do the oversight roles 91d12c8f added. Swap the decorator for the action check.
- direct-files has NO project branch: no authz action, no scope(), hand-rolled user_lab_unit_ids in raw SQL. A project-owned direct upload is reachable by lab assignment alone -- the AUTHZ-04 shape on the KPI surface. Move it onto the same actions and scope().

## Classification (by whether the query returns a record list)
Aggregates (8): year-month-wise-uploads, dr-reports-count, glaucoma-reports-count, images-count, dr-results-distribution, glaucoma-results-distribution, vcdr-distribution, direct-files/upload-metrics.
Record lists (4): encounter-files/filtered-dataframe(+excel), direct-files/filtered-dataframe(+excel).

## Open question
Whether .view staying project_gated=False is right for the CLINICAL aggregates (DR/glaucoma distributions, VCDR) as opposed to throughput. The _aggregate_kpi rationale -- 'a count of what a lab captured is a fact about that lab's own throughput' -- does not obviously cover a distribution of a project's clinical findings.

## Sweep
zip_filename is an identifier wherever it appears, not only in exports. Check verification screens, job status pages and search results for the same assumption.

title: Raw EXIF is retained on most ingestion paths and readable by fifteen roles
description:
Divergence D-29. A patient-identifier disclosure path outside the OCR system entirely.

## Path
- api/image_metadata.py serves media.metadata.read and media.metadata.process, both using MEDIA_IMAGE_ROLES -- 15 roles, every project role including collaborator and analytics_viewer, the two defined as never seeing identifiers.
- The default payload is technical only (dimensions, format, bit depth, luminance, DPI). With include_raw: true the response adds exif_json.
- utils/image_metadata.py::_extract_exif_json stores whatever EXIF the file carried.

## Inconsistent stripping
Strips EXIF: zip_processor.py, iitk_api_integration/service.py, encounter_sets/iitk_encounterset_zip_importer.py.
Does NOT: services/uploads/direct.py, direct_uploads/save_image.py, services/uploads/mobile.py, remidio_api_integration/ingest.py (zero strip_exif calls in each).

So images arriving by direct, mobile or Remidio API retain the camera's tags.

## Implementation
- Call strip_exif_data on every ingestion path.
- Confine include_raw to the roles that may read image identifiers.

## Verification
- Test: collaborator and analytics_viewer are denied include_raw.
- Test: each ingestion path stores no exif_json.
- SAMPLE EXISTING DATA FIRST: whether identifiers are actually present in retained exif_json has not been checked. If they are, existing rows need remediation, not just the code path. That sampling decides the true severity and should happen before this is scheduled.

See docs/policy/authorizations.md, divergence D-29.
notes:
CORRECTIONS 2026-08-26 (second adversarial review):

1. exif_present is now CONFINED, not open. Earlier note said the flag stays available to any image-authorized role; the policy was subsequently tightened -- exif_present and the raw tags are both confined to the identifier-reading roles (MEDIA_PII_ROLES plus dataset_creator). The flag says an image is unclean, which is only actionable by whoever may clean it.

2. This needs an ACTION SPLIT, not a role change (divergence D-38). api/image_metadata.py authorizes media.metadata.read once and then serves either technical metadata or, on include_raw, the EXIF tags. Technical metadata is legitimately readable by all of MEDIA_IMAGE_ROLES; the tags are not. No single role set on that one action satisfies both. Add a separate action for exif_present and raw tags.

3. shows_pii will NOT do this for you (divergence D-37). ActionPolicy.shows_pii and action_shows_pii() have no consumer outside authz/policies.py -- 19 actions are classified and nothing reads the classification. Do not close this by marking the action; enforce it with the role set on the split action.

title: An upload profile assignment authorizes uploading without any uploading role
description:
Divergence D-24. Found by adversarial review; the inverse of D-12/D-19 and missed when the register was written.

An upload must satisfy two bounds: an uploading role, and an upload profile assignment covering the target Lab Unit. The role bound is not enforced.

## Path
- auth/roles.py:144 global_uploader_or_project_assignment_required falls through to user_has_any_project_upload_assignment, which asks only whether an active assignment exists -- no role check.
- The mutation service then validates the assignment and the profile's clinical dimensions but never the actor's role (services/uploads/direct.py:93, upload_profiles/service.py:420).
- Assignment creation accepts any active user: upload_profiles/admin_service.py:1181 _validate_user_lab_assignment checks the user is active and the Lab Units valid, not that they hold an uploading role.
- Live POST route: /api/direct-uploads/uploads/web (api/direct_uploads.py:101).

## Consequence
An ordinary active user with no uploading role -- assigned to a profile by mistake, or by an over-broad access manager (see AUTHZ-03, fundus_img_xtract-yc0j) -- can ingest patient data.

## Implementation
Require an uploading role at the decorator AND in the mutation service; require one at assignment creation so the bad state cannot be created. Both bounds, both directions.

## Verification
Test: a user holding no uploading role but holding an active assignment is denied at the route and at the service. Test: assignment creation rejects a user with no uploading role. See docs/policy/authorizations.md, divergence D-24.

title: Bound uploading twice: upload profile for kind, upload grant for lab unit
description:
Divergences D-12, D-19, D-20. An upload is authorized by two independent bounds and both must hold; the role alone authorizes nothing.

D-19: auth/roles.py:156 short-circuits global_uploader_or_project_assignment_required on has_role('admin','fileUploader'), so a holder uploads any kind into any Lab Unit of any hospital with no assignment consulted. The three classical create actions -- upload.direct.create, upload.pregraded.create, upload.zip.create -- state the correct rule and have NO call sites outside authz/. They are registered, correct, and never invoked. Remove the short-circuit and wire the actions.

D-12: PROJECT_UPLOAD_GRANTS accepts PROJECT_ROLE and LEGACY_PROJECT_CAPABILITY alongside UPLOAD_PROFILE, so a project role grant carrying an uploading role authorizes ingestion with no profile. Drop both non-profile sources from the five project.upload.* policies. Browsing a project is not ingesting into it. (Depends on fundus_img_xtract-xwwk retiring the legacy capability rows.)

D-20: ProjectUploadProfileAssignment.lab_unit_id is NOT NULL, so an upload grant names exactly one Lab Unit and project-wide can only be approximated by enumerating every configured one. Make it nullable with NULL meaning project-wide, matching how ProjectRoleGrant records scope.

## Verification
Tests: fileUploader with no assignment denied classically; upload into an unassigned Lab Unit denied; project role grant alone denied for project.upload.*; a NULL-lab-unit assignment reaches every configured Lab Unit. See docs/policy/authorizations.md.
notes:
SETTLED 2026-08-26 after codex review. Break-glass DOES reach ingestion, including writing patient records.

Ordinary path: uploading role AND an active assignment covering the selected operation.
Break-glass: admin acts through ADMIN_GLOBAL WITHOUT a personal assignment.

Break-glass relieves exactly one requirement -- that the ACTOR hold an assignment. It waives nothing else: the selected profile must still be active and configured for the target project, Lab Unit, upload kind and clinical dimensions, and created records must still carry the authorized project.

TWO IMPLEMENTATION GAPS beyond adding admin/ADMIN_GLOBAL to the three create actions (divergence D-43):

1. No profile to resolve. upload_profiles/service.py::validate_upload_scope resolves profiles from the ACTOR's assignments. An admin under break-glass presents none, so the service finds nothing to validate. Needs a separate resolver that validates the SELECTED profile is active and configured for the target, rather than that the actor is assigned to it.

2. No recording. An earlier note here claimed removing the short-circuit routes admin 'through the engine where it is recorded'. That was wrong: authorize() emits no telemetry -- record_authorization_decision has exactly one caller outside its own module, media/routes.py:201. Break-glass ingestion writes patient records, so the caller must record the decision explicitly.

title: Split dataset assembly from release: dataset_creator curates, data_exporter releases
description:
Divergences D-9, D-17, D-18.

authz/policies.py::_curation sets project_roles={dataset_creator} for all six dataset actions, so release is not separated from assembly and data_exporter -- though named in dataset.export.create and .download -- reaches no project-owned data.

## Implementation
- Assembly (dataset_creator): curation.view, curation.update, finalize, delete
- Release (data_exporter): export.create, export.download, share.manage
- dataset_creator loses every release action
- data_exporter keeps curation.view -- a releaser must inspect what it releases
- Release carries project-wide scope exactly as curation does: a release may draw on part of a project's data or all of it
- datasets/routes.py:600 gates share OTP regeneration on dataset_creator; move to data_exporter
- D-18: only a curated and finalised dataset may be released. Share creation checks is_finalized at datasets/routes.py:352 and export is queued from a share, so the rule currently holds by accident of routing. Make it a precondition of the action.

One person may hold both roles; admin remains break-glass.

## Verification
Tests: dataset_creator denied on all three release actions; data_exporter denied on curate/finalize/delete; lab-unit-scoped grants denied on project-owned rows; unfinalised dataset cannot be exported or shared by any role.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-26: this bead's D-18 wording is withdrawn. It says the finalised rule holds 'by accident of routing'. It does not -- three paths check is_finalized independently and deliberately: datasets/routes.py:348 (share creation), analytics/route_dataset_curation.py:1470 (direct export), jobs/routes.py:249 (export regeneration).

The real gap is narrower: no ActionPolicy carries the precondition, so a fourth release path would have to remember it. Future-proofing debt, not a present hole. Verified directly rather than inherited from the earlier register.

title: Confine patient identifiers to the pre-grading roles
description:
Divergences D-22 and D-23.

D-22: f9e3ffa8 removed analytics_viewer from project.encountersets.browse_pii, stating 'authorization now agrees rather than leaving masking to do the work alone'. It was removed from authz/policies.py only. The live browser (remidio_api_integration/service.py::_apply_encounter_set_browser_scope) reads data_authorization.policy.ACTION_ROLE_NAMES, which still lists it. Nobody is exposed today -- both holders reach identifiers via another role -- but granting analytics_viewer to a user without a clinical role surfaces patient identifiers to a role defined as never seeing them.

D-23: browse_pii authorizes eleven roles including grading, discrepancy review, regrade adjudication, curation, export, and all three governance roles -- whose own definition at authz/policies.py:150 says 'None of it includes patient identifiers'.

## Implementation
Reduce browse_pii to the pre-grading set already encoded in MEDIA_PII_ROLES: admin, data_manager, fileUploader, local_admin, optometrist, verifier. Two definitions of who may see a patient identifier become one.

project.encountersets.browse is untouched -- every role keeps browsing, with identifiers masked.

## Verification
Assert browse_pii and MEDIA_PII_ROLES agree. Assert analytics_viewer is denied on both the authz path and the live browser path. Assert browse still admits all project-assignable roles.

title: Narrow verification authorization to verifier and admin
description:
Divergence D-7. Only verifier authorizes verification, with admin as break-glass.

VERIFICATION_ROLES drops fileUploader, local_admin and data_manager. Each held it by inheritance rather than by decision, and every additional holder is ambiguity about who is accountable for the judgement.

Rationale: an uploader may be a non-technical operator; deciding whether captured data is fit to become gradable work needs someone technical. Same cut as bda457bd (verifier off optometrist) and c92e875b (adjudication off data_manager).

## Ordering
BLOCKED on the verifier grant migration -- run that first or five users lose verification.

## Verification
Tests asserting fileUploader, local_admin and data_manager receive 403 on all seven verification.* actions, and verifier and admin still pass. See docs/policy/authorizations.md.

title: authz: fold data_authorization into authz as the single authorization module
description:
data_authorization/service.py's own docstring says the package 'is not a second policy decision engine'. data_authorization/policy.py is exactly that, and because the live routes call it rather than authz, it is the engine that actually decides.

The two are kept in step only by comments (authz/policies.py:358, authz/predicates.py:563 both say they 'mirror' it). They have already drifted.

## Why this is the root cause
Most findings in the authorization register are symptoms:
- D-1..D-4 (AUTHZ-03, fundus_img_xtract-yc0j): scope containment is stated correctly in authz via min_project_scope and never consulted, because grant management calls data_authorization.
- D-22: f9e3ffa8 removed analytics_viewer from project.encountersets.browse_pii and said 'authorization now agrees rather than leaving masking to do the work alone'. It was removed from authz only; the live browser reads data_authorization.policy.ACTION_ROLE_NAMES, which still lists it. Nobody is exposed today (both holders reach identifiers via another role) but the gap is live.

## Scope
- 19 user_can_project_action call sites across 10 files: remote_inference/manual_service.py, remote_inference/encounter_service.py, admin/upload_profiles.py, upload_profiles/admin_service.py, api/remidio_api_integration.py, api/ai_models.py, api/remote_inference.py, remidio_api_integration/service.py, remidio_api_uploads/encounter_set_browser.py, remidio_api_uploads/wadhwani_inference.py
- project_capabilities() rebuilt on authz
- ACTION_ROLE_NAMES deleted (authz.POLICIES is the map)
- PROJECT_ONLY_ROLE_NAMES and the role groups move to authz
- scope containment logic moves to authz; data_authorization keeps containment on write only

data_authorization retains what its docstring claims: the ProjectRoleGrant ORM, grant management with containment, and grant resolution feeding authz.

## Verification
Delete data_authorization/policy.py entirely. A test asserting no module outside data_authorization imports a decision function from it. Re-run the browse_pii comparison and confirm one role set, not two.

See docs/policy/authorizations.md divergence D-5.
notes:
ADVERSARIAL REVIEW 2026-08-26 -- two corrections to this bead.

1. Import count understated. '16 files' counted importers of data_authorization.policy specifically. Importers of the data_authorization package as a whole: 27 production files. The fold's surface is larger than stated.

2. The full-package fold is contested and the objection is sound enough to settle before starting. The reviewer argues: authz.engine and authz.policies remain separable evaluators even though resolver/predicates/cache touch SQLAlchemy; grant persistence and mutation are a legitimate separate boundary; and moving every ORM, CRUD and exception into one top-level package does not itself prevent a second policy engine appearing -- it risks a wide dependency hub mixing read-only evaluation with authority mutation.

The necessary and sufficient change is to dissolve data_authorization/policy.py as a DECISION engine and make every route/object/query consumer call one evaluator. Whether the ORM and grant CRUD also move is a separate question with no authorization consequence.

Also note: consolidating onto authz as it stands would swap one wrong answer for another. authz declares min_scope=PROJECT_SCOPE for both manage actions, which contradicts the containment model in the frozen policy. The rule must be written into authz first -- see divergence D-5.

title: AUTHZ-07: audit and S3 administration roles are broader than the admin-only policy
description:
From the route-by-route authorization audit (AUTHZ-07, High).

audit/routes.py and the S3 administration surface admit roles wider than docs/policy/admin_access_policy.md allows, and S3 status can be reached unscoped.

## Implementation
Narrow both surfaces to the documented admin-only policy and scope S3 status to the caller's authority.

## Verification
Tests asserting non-admin roles receive 403 on audit and S3 admin routes, and that S3 status is scoped.

title: AUTHZ-05: pregraded grade import route has no upload-profile or project authorization
description:
From the route-by-route authorization audit (AUTHZ-05, High, data exposure).

The pregraded grade import surface (direct_uploads/pregraded.py, direct_uploads/pregraded_grades.py) does not authorize the caller against an upload profile assignment or a project grant for the target project, so import can be driven against projects the caller has no relationship with.

## Implementation
Gate on project.upload.pregraded via data_authorization.policy.user_can_project_action, resolving project/hospital/lab from the target rather than trusting request fields.

## Verification
Tests: user with no pregraded upload assignment on the target project is denied; assigned uploader still succeeds; cross-project target is denied.
notes:
COMPOUNDED (2026-08-26, divergence D-31): the same route is gated on the wrong role as well as checking nothing about the target.

direct_uploads/pregraded_grades.py:713 and :1139 are @roles_required('fileUploader'). Ruling: pre-graded ingestion requires pregarded_uploader, in both classical and project contexts, because a pre-graded upload carries grades in with the images -- it asserts clinical findings rather than only capturing data. fileUploader does not confer it.

So the route currently admits the generic uploading role, excludes the role named for the work, and then performs no upload-profile or project authorization on the target. Fix both together: correct role AND the two bounds (profile decides the kind, grant decides the Lab Unit).

Also correct the actions: upload.pregraded.create accepts fileUploader alongside pregarded_uploader; project.upload.pregraded accepts nine roles including fileUploader, optometrist and verifier.

title: AUTHZ-06: ad-hoc task creation trusts client image refs and lab ids without resource-scope validation
description:
From the route-by-route authorization audit (AUTHZ-06, High, data exposure).

tasks/ad_hoc.py accepts client-supplied image references and lab unit ids and creates grading tasks without validating that those resources fall inside the caller's authorized scope. A caller can attach tasks to images outside their lab/project scope.

## Implementation
Resolve each supplied image ref to its owning project/hospital/lab (see data_authorization.policy.grading_task_project_scope for the resolution pattern) and authorize each before task creation; reject the request on any out-of-scope ref rather than silently skipping.

## Verification
Tests: out-of-scope image ref rejected; out-of-scope lab_unit_id rejected; in-scope creation still succeeds.

title: AUTHZ-04: EncounterSet verification mutations fall back to lab assignment for project-owned encounters
description:
From the route-by-route authorization audit (AUTHZ-04, High, data exposure).

verify_encounter_set/routes.py mutation paths authorize project-owned encounters via lab-unit assignment rather than requiring project authority. A user assigned to a lab unit can act on encounters owned by a project they hold no grant on, provided the encounter's lab unit overlaps their assignment.

## Implementation
Require project authority (data_authorization.policy.user_can_project_action) whenever the target encounter has a project_id; keep the lab-assignment path only for projectless legacy encounters.

## Verification
Tests: lab-assigned user without a project grant is denied on a project-owned EncounterSet mutation; projectless legacy path still works.

title: AUTHZ-03: scoped project_admin can widen role grants beyond its own scope
description:
From the route-by-route authorization audit (AUTHZ-03, High, privilege escalation).

docs/policy/authorizations.md:958 specifies that project.access.manage requires project_admin **through a project-wide role grant**. The code does not enforce the project-wide part.

data_authorization/service.py::_require_manage_scope accepts ANY active project_admin grant on the project, ignoring that grant's scope_type/hospital_id/lab_unit_id, and ignoring the scope of the grant being written. A hospital- or lab-unit-scoped project_admin can therefore mint project-scope operational grants for any user in the project, including themselves, across every configured lab unit.

_manageable_grant_clause has the same gap on the read/list side: any manager grant exposes every configured hospital and lab unit.

data_authorization/policy.py::_has_project_role and allowed_lab_unit_ids_for_action compound it: the PROJECT_WIDE_GOVERNANCE_ROLE_NAMES short-circuit promotes any project_admin/project_pi grant to project-wide regardless of its stored scope.

api/project_role_grants.py is @login_required only and takes scope_type/hospital_id/lab_unit_id straight from the client, so the service check is the only gate.

## Implementation
Make governance grant scope authoritative: require PROJECT_SCOPE for the manage path, and make the governance short-circuit scope-aware so narrow grants fall through to normal scope containment instead of being promoted.

## Verification
Tests covering: lab-scoped project_admin denied project-scope grant creation; denied cross-hospital grant creation; denied self-widening; project-scoped project_admin still works; narrow governance grants still authorize within their own scope for browse/view.

title: Grader responsiveness: bound queue scan, count KPIs in SQL, throttle session writes
description:
Grader responsiveness work (D2, D3, D12 of docs/15-DEVELOPMENT/grader_responsiveness_performance_plan.md).

## Results (local prod-restore: 27558 tasks, 7794 pending, 4 enforcement-enabled projects, user main_admin)

/grading page render: ~1.5s -> 0.259s. Per-disease cards now hydrate via HTMX.
Pending KPI, Glaucoma: 0.537s -> 0.033s. DR: 0.320s -> 0.042s. Counts bit-identical (5067/5340/22).
select_next_task Glaucoma resident: 0.504s -> 0.008s (63x). resident2: 0.231s -> 0.009s. ORDER BY random() removed (random_sorts=0).
EXPLAIN: enforced-project queue 2.29ms, legacy queue 1.60ms, both on ix_task_disease_lab_state.

## Implementation
- Migration 0d3edcf7bc3b: grading_tasks.project_id maintained by trigger, plus guard triggers on the 4 source tables refusing a project change while tasks reference the row. Backfill verified: 0 rows disagree with the Python resolver or the old 6-way COALESCE across all 27558 rows.
- exact_allocation_predicate()/project_enforces_allocation() in grading_allocation/dashboard.py express is_user_eligible_for_task in SQL, including its refusal when the target identity is unresolvable.
- _pending_count counts in SQL; _eligible_pending_tasks deleted.
- select_next_task filters in SQL, fetches ids, shuffles in Python, leases unchanged (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED).
- Dashboard KPI tiles removed; queue cards load per disease via /grading/fragments/disease-queue/<id> and /api/grading/me/queues[/<id>].
- server_side_session.py: session row rewritten only on material change or 60s expiry drift (30min timeout).

## Verification
- Equivalence: SQL filter vs is_user_eligible_for_task compared per candidate across all 15 queues for main_admin -> IDENTICAL everywhere, including Glaucoma legacy (5341 candidates, 0 eligible) and Glaucoma resident2 enforced-project (6181 candidates, 1658 eligible).
- 435 passed, 2 failed; both failures (test_wadhwani_glaucoma_batch) pre-exist on a clean tree.

## Not done
- D5/D6/D7 image tiering and cache headers: image files absent locally, cannot be reproduced or verified here.
- D1 production process model: local override is gitignored dev config; the deploy host must be checked separately.
- NOT COMMITTED at user request.
notes:
Browser-verified 2026-08-25 in Chrome against the running app:
- Reload with scroll restored: CLS 0, zero layout-shift entries, document height delta 0px.
- Refresh control: CLS 0, one click re-fetches all 6 disease cards + project panel with refresh=1, each swapping in place; counts never revert to placeholders.

title: Give field roles WAI/OCR inference access via lab-unit allocation
description:
Field optometrist/ophthalmologist need WAI inference and Remidio OCR results for their upload-profile lab units, and to request inference on their own encounters. Also fixes L19 (classical inference trigger had no lab scoping) and L24 (WAI statistics hospital-wide leak) from the authz audit.

## Implementation

The key constraint: automated Remidio API pulls have no uploading user by design, so ownership cannot gate access -- lab-unit allocation has to. Reach follows the same lab units an upload-profile assignment covers, regardless of which profile (manual or automated) ingested a given row, because the grant is (project, lab unit), not (project, lab unit, profile).

- authz/predicates.py: found and fixed a genuine engine/SQL disagreement -- the predicate compiler had no branch for GrantSource.UPLOAD_PROFILE, so authorize() allowed an assigned uploader's row while scope_query() hid it from every list screen. Added the branch, mirroring engine._matches_upload_profile via the existing _project_scope_match helper.
- authz/actions/inference.toml (new) + authz/policies.py: registered inference.wai.{summary,rows,retry,run}, all via a new _inference_step() policy shape -- same dual-branch reach as _reviewer_step, but with GrantSource.UPLOAD_PROFILE added and field roles deliberately NOT in owner_roles (ownership is a filter over this set, never the gate).
- authz/policies.py: flipped project.wai.run/project.wai.results from a project-wide gate to a lab-unit-scoped filter (moved GATE_ACTIONS -> FILTER_ACTIONS in tests/unit/authz/test_project_scope_levels.py to match) -- a lab-scoped grant now reaches its own lab instead of nothing.
- services/wai_api_statistics.py: replaced the broken scope clause. The old rule was '(hospital_id = X OR lab_unit_id IN (...))' -- the OR made the lab filter decorative, it fell back to the whole hospital when the user had zero lab units, and it never looked at project_id at all. Registered wai_api_statistics_rows_v as a lightweight authz-scoped table and now compile scope_query() into the raw SQL via literal_binds (every value is an integer id from resolved grants, never user input).
- api/ai_models.py: L19 fix -- infer_wadhwani_glaucoma_task's classical branch was 'has_role(admin, verifier, optometrist)' with zero lab scoping. Now goes through authorize() with the same inference.wai.run action as the project branch.
- api/wai_api_statistics.py, analytics/route_wai_api_statistics.py: widened read decorators to admin, local_admin, verifier, data_manager, analytics_viewer, optometrist, ophthalmologist, field_optometrist, field_ophthalmologist. Retry stays admin/local_admin/data_manager (spends an external API call).
- docs/policy/authorizations.md: documented all 4 new actions and the revised project.wai.* rules, including why reach is upload-profile-based rather than ownership-based.

## Verification

New tests: tests/unit/authz/test_upload_profile_parity.py (6 tests -- pins the UPLOAD_PROFILE parity fix, including the specific case of engine=True/sql=False the old code produced), tests/unit/authz/test_wai_inference_scope.py (20 tests -- pins lab-unit reach on both sides of the project boundary, the manual+automated-profile-same-lab case the requirement turns on, and that retry is narrower than read), tests/unit/services/test_wai_stats_scoping.py (4 tests -- executes the compiled SQL against a real database to prove it parses and actually restricts).

Full suite before/after, identical selection: 127 failed / 1657 passed / 74 errors both before and after this change (comm shows zero difference either direction). authz suite: 337/337 passing after updating the two tests whose fixtures encoded the old project.wai gate-not-filter behavior.

title: IITK incomplete-session signal is wrong and retry cannot reach late-uploaded images
description:
## Problems

Two, found by inspecting production data rather than reading code.

1. The incompleteness signal was wrong. local_image_count < source_image_count
   reported 253 of 335 sessions as incomplete. source_image_count comes from the
   session's own imageCount, which counts auxiliary artifacts such as 'consent'
   that /listImages never returns - documented in the April probe. Almost every
   COMPLETE session therefore looked short by one. The corrected signal (compare
   against the stored image inventory, plus upstream source_status == 'partial')
   gives 102, all of which are genuinely partial upstream.

   This signal was also used by field_workbench/sources/iitk.py, so the field app
   would have shown 253 incomplete sessions and offered a retry that could never
   reduce the number.

2. Retry could not reach late-uploaded images. _collect_sessions windows on
   last_success_at - 1 day, and the field retry just triggered an ordinary
   incremental sync. Sessions whose images are uploaded more than a day later
   were never re-listed. Real incomplete sessions here go back to 2026-08-01.

## Fix

- inventory_image_count / session_is_incomplete / list_incomplete_sessions /
  incomplete_session_count in iitk_api_integration.service own the correct rule.
- sync_config gains since_date; _collect_sessions honours it.
- resync_incomplete_sessions widens the window to the oldest still-incomplete
  session, capped at RESYNC_MAX_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 14. Uncapped, a permanently
  partial session would rescan weeks of history on every retry and spend the
  provider's ~60 req/min budget re-listing sessions that never change.
- resync_session(config_id, session_id) re-fetches one session directly, for the
  per-encounter refresh.
- New celery task resync_incomplete_iitk_sessions_task; the field adapter's retry
  now dispatches that instead of a plain incremental sync.

## Per-encounter refresh

field_service.refresh_encounter_from_source dispatches on the encounter's source:
IITK re-syncs the session, Remidio re-pulls the patient by MRN. Exposed twice from
one service - POST /api/mobile/v1/field/encounters/<uuid>/refresh (bearer) and
POST /api/encounter-sets/<uuid>/refresh-source (session), plus a 'Refresh from
source' button in the encounter-set browser details panel. Both share the field
throttle so a details panel cannot become a way around it.

The UI reports what the source returned and never concludes that nothing was
captured - we only observe upstream state, and images may be uploaded later. The
button stays enabled for the same reason.

## Verification

124 passed across field_workbench, iitk_api_integration, remidio_api_integration,
remidio_api_uploads. 5 new tests cover the corrected signal; 3 cover the refetch route.

Live test against encounter 3976 (project 5, 2026-08-19, IITK, 0 images): the source
currently reports status=partial, image_count=1, capturedPositions=('consent',) and
/listImages returns 0 images. resync_session re-queried, added nothing, and reported
honestly - exactly the intended behaviour for a session whose images are not
available upstream yet.

title: pull_latest_patient_exam blanks site_custom_identifier on existing staged exams
description:
## Problem

pull_latest_patient_exam blanked site_custom_identifier on any exam that a date
pull had already staged.

Two lines combined: the service passed extract_exam_payloads(site_custom_identifier=
None) because the getPatientWithLastExam response body carries no identifier, and
persistence.py assigned it unconditionally onto the existing row.

Confirmed live against the Comoph connection: exam 3171 went from comoph_4834 to
None after one re-pull. Routing survived because _site_identifier() falls back to
exam.site.site_custom_identifier and the site FK was still resolved from the numeric
site id - which is what made the corruption silent.

Latent, not active: only 1 row in the database has pull_source=getPatientWithLastExam
(my own test) and 0 exams have a NULL site_custom_identifier. The endpoint had never
been used in production, so the bug would have started corrupting rows the moment the
field re-pull feature shipped.

## Also confirmed by live probe

getPatientWithLastExam requires the NUMERIC Remidio site id, not the site custom
identifier, despite the vendor mail and the Postman path variable both naming it
siteCustomId. comoph_4834 -> 404; 5733647311175680 -> 200. This matches the
2026-04-30 probe in docs/16-NewFeature, so it is stable behaviour rather than a
one-off.

## Fix

- persistence.py no longer blanks a populated site_custom_identifier or
  remidio_numeric_site_id when a payload lacks one. Makes the class of bug
  impossible regardless of caller.
- service.py gains _site_custom_identifier_for(), resolving the identifier from
  RemidioSite by either numeric id or custom id, so pull_latest_patient_exam stages
  a correct identifier instead of None.

Restoration is automatic: re-pulling a damaged patient repairs the row as a side
effect. Verified live - exam 3171 went None -> comoph_4834 on the next pull. No
migration or repair script needed.

## Verification

tests/unit/remidio_api_integration/test_exam_upsert_identifier.py - 3 new tests.
75 passed across remidio_api_integration + remidio_api_uploads + iitk_api_integration.

Also fixed a pre-existing collection collision: those suites both define
test_client.py/test_service.py and had no __init__.py, so pytest could not collect
them together.

title: IITK-ingested images skip metadata extraction and PII detection
description:
## Problem

IITK-ingested EncounterSet images were written to disk but never had metadata
extracted or their pixels scanned for burned-in PII. _persist_session does EXIF
stripping, thumbnailing and file_hash inline, but never queued the Celery chain
that runs process_file_data_pipeline(run_metadata=True, run_pii=True) - which the
Remidio path has always queued via _queue_encounter_set_image_post_processing.

Consequence: no ImageMetadata row and no PiiVerification row for any IITK image.
EncounterSetImage.is_pii is hardcoded False at creation in this path, so nothing
ever revisited that assumption. IITK captures are 9-gaze closeup images from a
capture app, so burned-in patient identifiers are plausible.

Scope note: the missing AI-inference hook in this path is intentional - IITK has
no AI models configured (confirmed with the user). Only the image pipeline was
a bug.

## Fix

- New encounter_sets/post_processing.py::queue_image_post_processing(image_ids,
  user_id=None) holding the queueing logic, including the celery_enabled() inline
  fallback. Never raises: ingestion has already committed by then.
- remidio_api_integration._queue_encounter_set_image_post_processing now delegates
  to it, so both ingestion paths cannot drift.
- iitk_api_integration._persist_session tracks images that received bytes this run
  and queues them after the commit, so the worker cannot read rows that are not
  yet visible.

Only images that actually received new bytes are queued - a re-sync that downloads
nothing does not re-scan unchanged images.

## Verification

tests/unit/iitk_api_integration: 26 passed (2 new - one asserting downloaded images
are queued with their real ids, one asserting a no-download re-sync queues nothing).
tests/unit/remidio_api_integration + remidio_api_uploads: 46 passed, confirming the
delegation preserved Remidio behaviour.

title: Field staff API: project-scoped encounter queue, WAI status, Remidio/IITK fetch
description:
## Implementation

- policy.py: project scope from ProjectRoleGrant; unauthorized project returns 404 not 403.
- status.py: patient-level rollup of Remidio report + WAI DR/DME + WAI Glaucoma.
  DR/DME per-eye from the is_primary image (vendor contract); Glaucoma aggregated from
  task-scoped runs since it has no encounter-level run. Either eye positive => positive;
  both ungradable => not_gradable, never negative.
- sources/: adapters for Remidio (Job-based) and IITK (config-row lease). Fetch coalesces
  on an in-flight run, which is what actually bounds upstream load.
- cache.py: version-stamped Redis keys; the key carries a fingerprint of the caller's
  grants so a revoked grant cannot be served stale patient data.
- audit.py: rows for queue reads, detail reads, inference requests, fetch requests.
- throttle.py: 30s minimum gap per user (limiters express volume, not spacing).

Cache busting wired into: Remidio ingest, IITK _finish_sync, both WAI celery tasks
(including failure paths), OCR completion, verification/reopen, and project grant changes.

Removed the dead generate_mobile_token + POST /api/v1/encounter-set/upload and their
false-green tests (3 files deleted, 2 files trimmed).

## Fixes after review

- Celery dispatch deferred until after the request transaction commits (fetch + glaucoma);
  previously the worker could start before its rows were visible.
- remidio_report no longer downgrades a completed OCR status when a later attachment is
  still queued.
- is_positive_output and load_encounter made public rather than imported as privates.
- refresh_expires_in reports real expiry (Phase 0 carry-over).

## Known limitations

- Flask-Limiter has no storage in the test environment ('Limiter initialization failed.
  Storage is None'), so endpoint-level 2/min and 20/hr limits are not asserted by unit
  tests. Verified manually in the e2e walk against the running app, where the 30s spacing
  guard returned 429.
- Retry-After header carries the limiter's 60s window rather than the 30s spacing window;
  the message text avoids stating a contradicting number. Honouring the header is safe.
- Flask-Caching is a null cache under tests, so cache tests cover key derivation only.
  Read-back and version bump verified against the real app + Redis.

title: Phase 0: Mobile/desktop device enrolment gate and session hardening
description:
## Implementation

Device enrolment gate for the mobile/desktop bearer-token API, plus session hardening,
ahead of the field patient-data surface (blocks fundus_img_xtract-pf9w).

New deep module `mobile_devices/`:
- `MobileDevice` (user_id, device_id) unique, status pending|approved|blocked,
  device_kind personal|shared, platform android|ios|windows|macos|web.
- `MobileDeviceEnrolmentCode`: single-use, 30-min expiry, hashed at rest, bound to one user.

Gate wired into `services/mobile/auth_sessions.py`:
- login refuses to mint tokens unless the device is approved
- refresh revokes the session if the device was blocked since login
- validate_access_session re-checks device status every request, so blocking ends access
  at the next call rather than at token expiry

Hardening:
- refresh lifetime by device kind: shared 24h, personal+field role 7d, else 30d
- active-session cap policy-driven: 1 for field roles, 2 otherwise; displaced device gets
  `session_superseded` (new `mobile_auth_sessions.revoked_reason` column)
- `refresh_expires_in` now reports the session's real expiry (was hardcoded 30d - would
  have made shared devices refresh long after expiry)
- rate-limit key is mobile-aware (was Flask-Login only, so bearer clients all collapsed
  onto their IP); login additionally buckets per claimed username
- new field sessions refused with 503 when Redis (token denylist) is unreachable
- device refusals deliberately do NOT count toward account lockout

Roles: field_optometrist / field_ophthalmologist added to auth/roles.py DEFAULT_ROLES,
PROJECT_ASSIGNABLE_ROLE_NAMES, and CAPABILITY_ROLES[browse|verify].

Admin: enrolment-code issuing + approve/block panel in the user hub Sessions tab.

Migration b1c2d3e4f5a6 - creates both tables, adds revoked_reason, seeds the two roles,
and auto-approves every existing (user_id, device_id) so current uploaders are not locked
out on deploy. Upgrade/downgrade verified round-trip.

## Deviation from plan

Enrolment folded into POST /auth/login via an optional `enrolment_code` field rather than
a separate POST /devices/enrol. One screen, password verified once. Documented.

## Deferred

Audit rows moved to fundus_img_xtract-pf9w: they target field routes that do not exist yet.

## Verification

test_mobile_upload_options / test_mobile_pwa / mobile_devices. The 6 remaining failures

## Fix (2026-08-20, post-deploy correction)

decision); only human work should block reopening.

- verify_encounter_set/reopen_service.py: HUMAN_GRADE_ROLE_SLOTS =
  ('resident','resident2','arbitrator','review') - guard now only blocks on Grade rows
  with a human role_slot, not 'ai'.
- verify_encounter_set/routes.py reopen_verification: also resets any
  EncounterAIInferenceRun row for the encounter (remote_inference/models.py - a
  DIFFERENT, durable idempotency table from AIInferenceRun, tracks the actual external
  AI request/response) from a blocking status (queued/presigning/uploading/submitting/
  success/partial) to 'failed'. Without this, enqueue_automatic_encounters() would see
  the orphaned prior run and silently skip re-queuing AI grading on re-finalize, even
  though the AI-graded tasks were just deleted. 'failed' reuses the existing
  retry-eligible status (dr_dme_service.py already retries runs in this state).

No schema change - code-only fix in the running route/service, requires 'make restart'
to take effect in production (templates hot-reload but Python does not).

New test: test_reopen_verification_allowed_with_only_ai_grade - reopen succeeds with
only an ai-role grade present, and the EncounterAIInferenceRun flips to failed.

title: No audit trail for EncounterSet verification metadata edits
description:
## Problem
verify_encounter_set.update_metadata overwrites EncounterSetImage.metadata_json and
PatientEncounters.metadata_json fields in place with no history kept. Confirmed no
audit/review_history/event-listener hooks cover this route.

Concretely: EncounterSetImage.metadata_json['laterality'] is set at Remidio ingestion
(remidio_api_integration/mapper.py:105) and the same key is now editable during
verification (fundus_img_xtract-mf2j added a Laterality/Focus row). Correcting it during
verification permanently replaces the ingested value - no prior value, no who/when.
Same applies to referral_needed_or_positive_image and every field in the admin-configured
editable_fields_by_scope.

## Impact
Clinical data system holding real patient images. If a verifier mis-corrects laterality
or any field, or if a correction is later disputed, there is no way to see what the
system originally recorded or who changed it.

## Suggested approach
Add a lightweight audit log (table or JSON diff) recorded in
verify_encounter_set.update_metadata's transaction: encounter_id/image_id, field key,
old value, new value, user, timestamp. Scope only to this route to start; broader
audit coverage is a separate decision.

title: Optimize grading workbench save and next-case latency
description:
## Evidence
Nine consecutive grading submissions executed 697-908 SQL statements each (median 766). Representative c81cfe66 used 697 statements and 340.6 ms DB execution; accepted persistence completed about 1.1 seconds before the POST response while synchronous next-work reservation/build continued. The browser then waits 450 ms and performs a GET that rebuilds the DTO. Draft autosaves execute 131-197 statements each; one 11-save workbench generated 1,925 statements.

## Cause
Drafts rebuild authoritative configuration and repeatedly resolve shared profile/policy graphs. Final submit synchronously acquires and fully builds the next DTO, returns it unused, then GET builds it again. Debug caller inspection amplifies the query fan-out. Successful request duration is computed but not logged.

## Plan
See docs/15-DEVELOPMENT/grading_workbench_save_latency_plan.md. Implement measurement first, then lightweight draft validation, split next-session reservation from DTO construction, batch resolver/builder reads, optimize queue/logging overhead, and consider full-workspace HTMX only if server-side work remains above target.

## Status
Implementation intentionally deferred to the next session. Preserve atomic submission, stable idempotency, no automatic final POST retry, GET-only Back/Forward, CSRF, authorization, configuration drift, audit, consensus, and lease correctness.

- Centralized BFCache handling in the shared submission guard: hide cached content before repaint and perform a fresh GET on Back or Forward.

## Implementation
Use the authorized stored queue directly for next navigation; add a per-render UUID4 review submission token backed by the unique review submission history request ID; serialize task writes and return prior success for same-user/task token replays; reset submission UI on pageshow; debounce refresh requests to one scheduled generation; use concurrent per-disease MV refresh with unique task indexes; document the form and refresh contracts.

title: Retry failed Wadhwani items after final pass delay
description:
## Problem
Concurrency three improved throughput but a 100-image batch received three intermittent Wadhwani HTTP 503 failures. The user requested initial concurrency two followed by two final retry passes.

## Implementation
Process the original batch with concurrency two. If failures remain, perform up to two retry passes. Each retry pass waits five seconds before starting, processes failed items serially, waits two seconds between retry items, and stops early once all failures recover. Final job status reflects the last retry outcomes.

## Verification
Thirteen focused Wadhwani task/client/inference tests pass in Compose. Tests cover maximum initial concurrency two, no retry delay when all succeed, early stop after recovery, two persistent-failure passes, serial retries, and two-second item gaps. Changed module compiles. General worker confirmed idle before restart.

title: Process Wadhwani batches with concurrency three
description:
## Problem
The general worker runs with Celery's solo pool, so its advertised concurrency does not parallelize the serial loop inside a Wadhwani batch. The observed 100-image batch had an early transient slowdown near 20.5 seconds per item before recovering; it ultimately completed 100/100 in about 13.7 minutes with a 2.1-second median.

## Image size analysis
The slow batch contained 100 local Pregraded images: 5.13-6.15 MB, median 5.23 MB, mean 5.39 MB. The preceding fast local Pregraded batch had median 5.24 MB and mean 3.89 MB. The 39 percent mean-size increase could not explain the greater-than-tenfold early latency increase; timing recovery within the same batch confirmed transient remote/network latency.

## Implementation
Use a bounded three-thread executor only inside the Wadhwani batch task, keep other general-worker queues serial, use thread-local pooled HTTP sessions, preserve per-item state and final job status, and contain unexpected per-item exceptions without persisting or logging exception text.

## Verification
Eleven focused Wadhwani task/client/inference tests pass in Compose, proving maximum parallelism three, correct status/error aggregation, and per-thread HTTP session isolation. Changed modules compile. Restart the general worker only after the active batch is idle.

title: Stop completed Wadhwani job polling
description:
## Problem
Completed image-based Wadhwani job pages kept issuing HTMX status XHRs. Removing hx-trigger after swap did not cancel HTMX's already-registered interval. The project-based job page used the same pattern, and both polled every two seconds.

## Implementation
Return HTMX status 286 from both Wadhwani status-fragment routes when the payload is terminal, preserving the final fragment swap while cancelling the registered polling trigger. Slow active polling on both job pages from every two seconds to every five seconds.

## Verification
Seven focused Wadhwani grading/EncounterSet tests pass in Compose, covering active 200, terminal 286, final done marker, and five-second markup on both pages. Both changed Python modules compile.

title: Harden Wadhwani S3 uploads against transient DNS
description:
## Problem
A 100-image Wadhwani batch completed 95 tasks but five S3 uploads failed during intermittent DNS resolution of glycoma-images.s3.amazonaws.com. Current requests.put created a fresh session and exposed the full presigned URL in RequestException text stored in job details.

## Implementation
Reuse a process-local HTTPS connection pool for Wadhwani requests, retry only idempotent S3 PUT uploads up to three times with bounded backoff for transient connection/DNS, throttling, and server failures, and sanitize upload failure messages so presigned URLs are not persisted or rendered.

## Verification
Eight focused Wadhwani client/inference tests pass in Compose. Changed module compiles. The general Celery worker was idle, restarted successfully without restarting web, responds to inspect ping, and reports retries=3, pool maxsize=8, allowed_methods=PUT.

title: Finalize project authorization deep module
description:
## Design

Use the global roles catalog as the single vocabulary. ProjectRoleGrant assigns one catalog role to a user within exactly one project-wide, hospital, or lab-unit scope. The first active grant is membership; no duplicate can_* booleans or separate membership approval. Project grants never populate global user_roles. Classical project_id NULL data remains governed by classical global roles and hospital/lab scoping.

## Implementation

Added the data_authorization deep module, idempotent migration/backfill, role-grant REST API, scoped manager rules, role/scope DTOs, compatibility checks for existing EncounterSet capability callers, and coarse route gates that still require object-level scope. Replaced the Project Access capability matrix with grouped user, Hospital/Lab unit, Grants/Roles, Edit rows. A manager can change scope/roles, remove one grant directly, or clear an assignment. All grant state mutations use inactive history rather than deletion and emit sanitized structured project_authorization logger records.

Kept non-project EncounterSets on classical scoping and project EncounterSets on explicit project grants/legacy compatibility rows, combined without cross-scope leakage. Project-only collaborators can use the no-PII browser without receiving a global collaborator role. PII workflow boundaries remain processing/verification plus the sole scoped EMR export exception.

## Verification

Focused PostgreSQL tests passed for role-catalog reuse, grant-created membership, project/site/lab containment, multiple roles, inactive grants, scope moves, direct removal, mutation logging, classical/project query separation, API and rendered workspace behavior, no-PII project-only collaborator access/redaction, media access, and verification route regressions. Alembic current and heads both report 7cb461952afe.
